business_problem: The incumbent relational database lacked scalability and impacted performance Agibank is on an impressive growth trajectory, aiming to expand its network to over two thousand branches by 2027.
solution_summary: The incumbent relational database lacked scalability and impacted performance Agibank is on an impressive growth trajectory, aiming to expand its network to over two thousand branches by 2027. Simplifying data management and enhancing security In 2022, Agibank implemented MongoDB Atlas on AWS and migrated its ECM system. To achieve this goal, the institution needs robust and scalable technology underpinning daily and critical operations. This is handled by the enterprise content management (ECM) system, which stores customer records such as tax and identification documents, photos, and biometric data. It was inflexible, with different schemas requiring different databases, and suffered from latency when executing tasks. The database also couldn’t support secondary indexes or full-text search, impacting the sales of core offerings, such as credit and loans, insurance, and credit card approvals.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the operational, document, and context data behind Agibank's document-heavy operational workflows.

data_flow: Application, customer, and workflow data is consolidated in MongoDB Atlas, indexed or enriched where needed, and then delivered to downstream applications, analytics, or AI features through low-latency queries and APIs. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, Azure, APIs.
business_outcome: Optimizing resources and improving operational efficiency With MongoDB Atlas, Agibank now has a high-performing, scalable, and resilient database platform underpinning its ECM system.
metrics: It’s 4.8 times faster than PostgreSQL and 90% more cost-effective,” adds Lanzarini.
